mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q01.stem: Inspection-passed products were scratched in transport and the specified quantity was short. What is appropriate?
options: No quality issue exists because manufacturing inspection passed.
Include logistics quality and investigate manufacturing and shipping histories separately.
Quantity is not a customer requirement.
Scratches become irrelevant once delivered.
reasons: Post-inspection scratches and supply conditions also concern customer requirements.
Check condition, quantity and shipping processes as quality.
Specified quantity is a logistics requirement.
Condition up to delivery also concerns quality.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q02.stem: Wastewater pH was measured. What is appropriate about COD or metal concentration?
options: Every value was obtained simultaneously.
Transparency eliminates other analyses.
All indicators have the same number and unit.
They concern different targets and need separate appropriate measurements.
reasons: pH itself is not the amount of other constituents.
Dissolved substances may not be visible.
Separate quantities, units and targets.
pH, oxygen demand and metal amounts provide different information.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q03.stem: Paper burette readings are initial 2.6 mL and final 17.4 mL. What volume was used?
options: 2.6 mL
reasons: The final reading alone is not used volume.
Do not add initial and final readings.
The initial reading alone is not used volume either.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q04.stem: A bath analysis sheet records only acid concentration. How should metal constituents be handled?
options: Determine every metal concentration from the acid value.
Suitable acid guarantees suitable metals.
Compare necessary constituents and analytical methods.
Matching color removes the need for values.
reasons: One result cannot determine a different target quantity.
Acidity control and metal-constituent control are separate.
Confirm what the result quantified.
Color cannot determine every constituent's amount.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q05.stem: Two paints have the same resin name. What is needed before a change?
options: Every product is interchangeable if the resin name matches.
Check only color.
Use any leftover hardener.
Compare the product-specified substrate, combinations and curing conditions.
reasons: Resin name alone does not determine formulation or application.
Performance and conditions extend beyond color.
Use the specified hardener combination.
Check classification together with individual product conditions.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q06.stem: Which statement about hard-anodized coating post-treatment is appropriate?
options: Prohibit sealing for every product.
Check wear/corrosion requirements and the application specification.
Thickness unconditionally guarantees withstand voltage.
Use representative values alone for human shock protection.
reasons: Applicability depends on requirements and specifications.
Consider tradeoffs among properties.
Defects, shape and test conditions also affect performance.
Representative values are not human-protection guarantees.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q07.stem: Two compounds are blue. Which selection is appropriate?
options: Matching color guarantees identical composition.
Use both for every rough-polishing process.
Compare item number, particles, specified use and work material.
Mixing guarantees interchangeability.
reasons: Color alone cannot establish composition or fineness.
Check use by product and combination.
Check product information and compatibility rather than nicknames.
Mixing does not establish compatibility and must not be unauthorized.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q08.stem: Which explanation separates design and manufacturing quality?
options: Separate setting a target from realizing it in the product.
Both mean only logistics delivery dates.
Ease of manufacture alone permits changing customer requirements.
Operators choose all inspection items by preference.
reasons: Distinguish the target from its realization and connect requirements.
Design and manufacturing do not mean only delivery time.
Do not confuse customer requirements with manufacturing convenience.
Inspection follows approved requirements and plans.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q09.stem: Which statement about equipment emissions and surrounding-environment evaluation is appropriate?
options: They are one identical number, so no target is needed.
Weak smell means every environment is safe.
Wastewater alone also reveals noise.
Separate what and where you evaluate, and check applicable conditions.
reasons: Targets, locations and methods differ.
Senses alone do not guarantee harmlessness.
Impact pathways and quantities differ.
Manage sources separately from environmental conditions.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q10.stem: An analog scale has 5 intervals between 10 and 20. What is one division?
reasons: Difference 10 divided by 5 intervals gives 2.
This uses the interval count as the value.
The numbered difference covers all intervals.
Do not multiply the difference by the interval count.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q11.stem: A solid appears in liquid. Which analytical approach is appropriate?
options: Every solid is metal electrodeposition.
Every white solid is the same compound.
Investigate precipitation, electrode deposition, cooling and other conditions separately.
Add reagent without recording anything.
reasons: There is more than one solid-forming pathway.
Different substances can look similar.
Combine appearance with formation conditions.
Do not add to unconfirmed liquids without authorization.

mfg1-surface-weekly-10-q12.stem: Which check is appropriate when using liquid polishing compound?
options: Liquid never splashes.
Check supply method, spray/cleaning and particle compatibility.
Soft buffs eliminate foreign-matter effects.
Color can replace the item number.
reasons: Liquid also requires spray controls.
Compare format, particles and supply separately.
Coarse particles or foreign matter can scratch even with a soft buff.
Do not identify a product by color alone.
